The State Of West Bengal & Ors vs Gurucharan Hansda & Ors
on 19 July, 2023
Author: Debangsu Basak

entities.text: State Of West Bengal & Ors vs Gurucharan Hansda & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Bench: Debangsu Basak 19.07.2023 Item No.2 Ct. No.5 CHC (dismissed)
 F.M.A. 534 of 2023  IA NO: CAN/2/2023  The State of West Bengal & ors.
 Vs.
 Gurucharan Hansda & ors.
 Mr. Susovan Sengupta, Ld. A.G.P.
 Mr. Sanatan Panja  ...for the appellants  Mr. Bhagbat Chowdhury,
 Mr. Dilip Kumar Sadhu  ...for the respondents/writ petitioners

The appeal is at the behest of the State, and is directed against an order dated April 6,
2022 passed in WPA 15370 of 2017.
Learned advocate for the State contends that, the plots involved stood vested within the State under the provisions of the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1958 and in support of such contention reliance was placed on the writing at page 15 of the stay petition.

entities.text: West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1958
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore the impugned order was incorrect.
The records produced demonstrate that four plots of land are involved.
State filed an affidavit before the trial Court where State took the stand that the plots were acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Possession of the plots were taken by the State.
No compensation was paid to the private respondents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By the impugned order the learned Trial Judge after noting that the acquisition proceeding did not result in an award, and that possession, of the plots were with the State, directed the State to earlier purchase the two plots directly from the private respondents or invoke the Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 within three months.

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: We find no merit in the present appeal.
The plots belong to the private respondents.
Vesting under the Act of 1956 does not takes place.
What is permissible under the Act of 1956 is acquisition which was not done in the facts of the present case although the State is in possession.
Therefore, no infirmity can be found from the direction issued by the learned Trial Judge by the impugned order.
The appeal is dismissed with exemplary costs of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh) to be paid by the deponent of the application.
Such person is at liberty to reimburse himself of the same from the person responsible, if there be any other apart from him.
F.M.A. 534 of 2023 along with connected application are dismissed.

(Debangsu Basak, J.) (Md. Shabbar Rashidi, J.)
